topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by setting out the learning outcomes and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular cascades drive growth signal autonomy and evade growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how failure to exit the cell cycle and complete terminal differentiation maintains proliferative capacity in hematopoietic and epithelial malignancies.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis and regulation of cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the molecular mechanisms and balance between pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic factors that allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and cellular stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere biology, telomerase reactivation, and p53-mediated stress pathways govern cellular senescence and immortalization.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways such as aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations drive oncogenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how the angiogenic switch and blood vessel recruitment provide oxygen and nutrients essential for tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the sequential barriers, circulatory dissemination, clinical monitoring, and genomic characteristics of metastatic cancer cells.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the overarching concept of cancer hallmarks and directing students to upcoming sessions.
